pages.title: 01 // THE DRIFT NIGHTMARE
pages.content:
A web app crashes? You get a 500 error. You fix a line of code.

An autonomous bipedal robot drifts in physical space? 0.01% spatial memory error means a 50kg arm smashes into an assembly line.

In web dev, drift is annoying. In Physical AI, drift is catastrophic. You cannot rely on 2D camera feeds. You need 3D LiDAR spatial point clouds streaming at 60 FPS.

pages.title: 02 // THE NEURAL PIPELINE
pages.content:
How do you eliminate physical memory drift? You build a zero-drift ingestion pipeline.

LiDAR spatial stream -> Neural Processing Core -> Motor & Hand Actuation.
Inference latency: 1.8ms.
Ingestion speed: 60 FPS dataset stream.
Tactile force matrix: 1,024 active nodes.

Your cursor becomes a magnetic attractor. It bends the point cloud in real time. You see the data stream move before the robot acts.

pages.title: 03 // LIVE ROS2 & PYTHON SANDBOX
pages.content:
A manager wants a dashboard. An engineer wants an API. We give them both.

Floating Glassmorphic Telemetry Dock at the top. Live ROS2 and Python Sandbox at the bottom. Don't hide the code behind flashy animations. Expose the SDK. Let developers test motor joint angles directly.

Control the point cloud stream. Control physical reality.
pages.code:
import rclpy
from physical_ai import MotorKinematics

robot = MotorKinematics(node_id="biped-arm-01")
robot.set_joint_angle(joint=3, angle=45.2, torque_limit=45.0)
assert robot.telemetry.latency < 2.0  # 1.8ms SLA
